reason: The text depicts Joseph's brothers as respectful and submissive toward Joseph, who holds authority in Egypt. When they encounter Joseph, they bow down to him (וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ לוֹ אַפַּיִם אָֽרְצָה). While Joseph speaks harshly to them (וַיְדַבֵּר אִתָּם קָשׁוֹת), the brothers respond with fear and deference, not antagonism. They are intimidated and compliant throughout the narrative. Even when falsely accused of being spies, they defend themselves respectfully rather than displaying antagonism. When Joseph's identity is finally revealed, they are shocked and emotionally moved, eventually drawing close to him. There is no evidence of the regular people (the brothers) being antagonistic toward their leader (Joseph).
